title: Definition
body_md:
A graph $G$ is \emph{Hamiltonian-transitive} if it is Hamiltonian and, for every pair of Hamiltonian cycles, there is an automorphism of $G$ that maps one cycle to the other.
	We denote the class of all Hamiltonian-transitive graphs by~$\mathcal{H}$.
head: environment

label: thm:odd-cayley-graphs
title: Theorem
head: environment

label: thm:cayley_even
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:cayley_even}
	Let $G$ be the Cayley graph of an abelian group w.r.t.~some generating set~$S$ and assume that $n:=|G|\geq 4$ is even.
	Moreover, assume that there is some~$s \in S$ such that $S\setminus \{s,-s\}$ is non-generating.
	Then $G \in \mathcal{H}$ if and only if~\hbox{$G \in \{C_n, C_4 \operatorname{\square} K_2, K_{3,3},  K_{4,4}\}$} or~$G=C_k \operatorname{\square} K_2$ where $k=n/2$ is odd.
head: environment

label: thm:cart-prod
title: Theorem
head: environment

label: lem:prime-not-in-H
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:prime-not-in-H}
	Let~\(G\) and~\(H\) be Hamiltonian graphs. If~\(G\) and~\(H\) are relatively prime, then~\(G \operatorname{\square} H \not \in \mathcal{H}\).
head: environment

label: lem:cart-prod-power
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:cart-prod-power}
	Let~\(G\) be a Hamiltonian and prime graph. Then~\(G^{\operatorname{\square} n} \not \in \mathcal{H}\) for all~\(n \geq 2\).
head: environment

label: cor:cart-prod-decomp
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:cart-prod-decomp}
	Let~\(G\) be a graph with decomposition~\(G=H_1^{\operatorname{\square} r_1}  \operatorname{\square} \dots \operatorname{\square} H_k^{\operatorname{\square} r_k}\) for pairwise distinct prime graphs \(H_1, \dots, H_k\). Assume that \(H_1,\dots,H_k \) are Hamiltonian. Then \(G \in \mathcal{H}\) if and only if~\(G=H_1 \in \mathcal{H}\).
head: environment

label: thm:cartesian-product-K2
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:cartesian-product-K2}
	Let~\(G\) be a Hamiltonian graph. Then~\(G \operatorname{\square} K_2 \in \mathcal{H}\) if and only if~\(G = C_k\) for~\(k \geq 3\) odd or~$G=C_4$.
head: environment

label: lem:oddcycle_prism
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:oddcycle_prism}
	Let $k\geq 3$ be odd. Then $C_k \operatorname{\square} K_2 \in \mathcal{H}$.
head: environment

label: lem:cartesian-K2-even
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:cartesian-K2-even}
	Let $G$ be Hamiltonian with $k:=|G|\geq 6$ even. Then $G \operatorname{\square} K_2 \notin \mathcal{H}$.

title: Remark
body_md:
Note that $C_k \operatorname{\square} K_2= \operatorname{Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_k \operatorname{\square} \mathbb{Z}_2, \{(0,1), (1,0), (0,-1), (-1,0)\})$. 
	In particular, it is the Cayley graph of an abelian group.
	If $k$ is odd, $C_k \operatorname{\square} K_2$ is generated by~$(1,1)$ so that  $C_k \operatorname{\square} K_2$ is even the Cayley graph of a cyclic group.
	On the other hand, note that for $k$ even, $C_k \operatorname{\square} K_2$ is not the Cayley graph of a cyclic group: To see this, assume that~$C_k \operatorname{\square} K_2 = \operatorname{Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{2k}, S)$ for some generating set $S$. Since  $C_k \operatorname{\square} K_2 = \operatorname{Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{2k}, S)$ is 3-regular,~$S$ contains the only self-inverse element of $\mathbb{Z}_{2k}$, i.e., $k$, and only one other element~$s$. 
	Then~$s$ is odd, because otherwise $S$ is not generating.
	Observe that $(0, s, 2s, \dots, ks, ks+k)$ is a closed walk of length $k+1$ because \(k\cdot s +k \equiv (s+1)k \equiv 0 \bmod 2k\). 
	This means that~$\operatorname{Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{2k}, S)$ contains a closed walk of odd length.
	Since the $k$-prism for $k$ even is bipartite with bipartition $A=\{u_i: i \text{ odd}\} \cup \{v_i: i \text{ even}\}$, $B=V\setminus A$, this gives a contradiction.

label: lemma:splittingcayley
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:splittingcayley}
	Let \(\Gamma_1\) and \(\Gamma_2\) be finite groups with generating sets \(S_1\) and \(S_2\), respectively. For \(\Gamma = \Gamma_1 \times \Gamma_2\), we have \(\operatorname{Cay}(\Gamma,S_1 \cup S_2) \cong \operatorname{Cay}(\Gamma_1, S_1) \operatorname{\square} \operatorname{Cay}(\Gamma_2, S_2)\).
head: environment

label: lemma:samekappa
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:samekappa}
	Let $G$ be a graph. If $G \in \mathcal{H}$, then all Hamiltonian cycles of $G$ have the same Hamilton compression.
head: environment

label: lemma:compositeorder
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:compositeorder}
	Let $\Gamma$ be an abelian group and \(p\) be a prime divisor of \(|\Gamma|\). Let \(S\) be a generating set of $\Gamma$ such that the order of each element in $S$ is either a power of $p$ or coprime to $p$.	
	Setting \(S_p:= \{s \in S \colon p \mid \operatorname{ord}(s)\}\) 
	and \(S'_{p} := S \setminus S_p\), we have~\(\Gamma = \langle S_p \rangle \times \langle S'_{p} \rangle\).

name: Layer structure

label: def:zigzag
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:zigzag}
	Assume that $G$ has $K$-$l$-layer structure with $l\geq 5$ odd and set $k := |K|$. Let~$C_K = (v_0, \dots, v_{k-1})$ be a Hamiltonian cycle of $K$.
	Given a tuple~$\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{a}} = (a_1, a_2, \dots, a_{(l-3)/2}) \in \{0, \dots, k-2\}^{(l-3)/2}$, we define the \emph{$C_K$-$\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{a}}$-zigzag cycle} as the Hamiltonian cycle illustrated in \cref{fig:zigzag}.
	For a zigzag cycle $C$, we define $\mu(C)$ to be the number of edges in the segment between \(v_{0,k-2}\) and \(v_{l-1,k-1}\) that contains vertex $v_{1,0}$, i.e., the length of the segment consisting of the green, pink, and orange line segments in \cref{fig:zigzag}.

label: obs:group-induced-layer
title: Observation
body_md:
\label{obs:group-induced-layer}
	Let $G$ be the Cayley graph of an abelian group $\Gamma$ with generating set $S$.
	Assume there is~$S'\subseteq S$ such that $\langle S' \rangle \cap S = S'$ and $|\langle S' \rangle|\geq 3$.
	Let $\Delta:=\langle S' \rangle$, $K:=\operatorname{Cay}(\Delta, S')$ and~$l:=|\Gamma:\Delta|$.
	Then $G$ has $K$-$l$-layer structure (\cref{def:layer-structure}), where the layers are given by the cosets of $\Delta$.
	We call such a layer structure \textit{group-induced}.
head: environment

label: lemma:layercayley
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:layercayley}
	Let $\Gamma$ be an abelian group of odd order with generating set $S$. Suppose that the Cayley graph $G = \operatorname{Cay}(\Gamma, S)$ is Hamiltonian-transitive and $\kappa(G) > 1$.
	Assume that $G$ has a group-induced $K$-$l$-layer structure with $|K|,l\geq 5$.
	Then $K$ is complete or a cycle.
head: environment

label: lemma:cayleycomplete
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:cayleycomplete}
	Let $\Gamma$ be an abelian group with generating set $S$. 
	Suppose that the Cayley graph~$G = \operatorname{Cay}(\Gamma,S)$ is Hamiltonian-transitive and  $\kappa(G) > 1$.
	Assume that $G$ has a group-induced $K$-$l$-layer structure where $K$ is a complete graph with $|K|\geq 5$.
	Then $G$ is complete.

label: lemma:cayleythreelayers
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:cayleythreelayers}
Let $\Gamma$ be an abelian group of odd order with generating set $S$. 
Suppose that the Cayley graph $G = \operatorname{Cay}(\Gamma,S)$ is Hamiltonian-transitive and  $\kappa(G) > 1$.
Assume that, for all~$s\in S$, $\operatorname{ord}(s)<5$ or $|\Gamma : \langle s\rangle|<5$.
Then~$\Gamma=\mathbb{Z}_3^d$ for $d\geq4$ or $G$ is complete or a~cycle.
head: environment

label: thm:main_cayley
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{thm:main_cayley}
	Let $\Gamma$ be an abelian group of even order with generating set $S$ and~${G = \operatorname{Cay}(\Gamma,S)}$. Suppose there exists an $s \in S$ such that \(l = |\Gamma:\langle S \setminus \{\pm s\} \rangle| \geq 4.\) Then $G \in \mathcal{H}$ if and only if~$G = C_n$ or $G = C_l \operatorname{\square} K_2$, where $l$ is odd or $l=4$.
head: environment

label: lemma:l=2
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:l=2}
	Let $\Gamma$ be an abelian group with generating set $S$ and $G = \operatorname{Cay}(\Gamma,S)$. Suppose that there exists an $s \in S$ such that \(l = |\Gamma:\langle S \setminus \{\pm s\} \rangle| =2.\) Then $G \in \mathcal{H}$ if and only if~$G \in \{C_4, K_{4,4}\}$ or $G = C_k \operatorname{\square} K_2$, where $k$ is odd or $k=4$.
head: environment

label: lemma:l=3
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:l=3}
	Let $\Gamma$ be an abelian group of even order with generating set $S$ and~${G= \operatorname{Cay}(\Gamma,S)}$. Suppose there exists an $s \in S$ such that \(l = |\Gamma:\langle S \setminus \{\pm s\} \rangle| =3.\) Then $G \in \mathcal{H}$ if and only if~$G \in \{K_{3,3}, C_3 \operatorname{\square} K_2\}$.
head: environment

label: rem:reg-graphs-in-H
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:reg-graphs-in-H}
	For every \(d \geq 2\), there are infinitely many \(d\)-regular Hamiltonian-transitive graphs in \(\mathcal{H}\): We construct such graphs as follows. For an arbitrary $n\geq 3$, take \(C_n\) and \(n\) disjoint copies of \(K_{d+1}\). 
	Remove one edge from each copy of \(K_{d+1}\) and replace each vertex~$v$ of \(C_n\) by a copy of \(K_{d+1}\) such that the two incident edges to $v$ are now incident to the two vertices of degree \(d-1\). See~\Cref{fig:constr-d-reg} for an illustration.
	This yields a \(d\)-regular Hamiltonian graph. It is Hamiltonian-transitive because every Hamiltonian cycle uses all of the edges of~$C_n$ and visits the vertices in each copy of $K_{d+1}$ in some arbitrary order. It is immediate that this order can be permuted by applying an automorphism.
head: environment

label: thm:cub-graphs-in-H
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{thm:cub-graphs-in-H}	
	There exists a family of cubic 3-connected Hamiltonian-tran\-si\-tive graphs with an unbounded number of edge orbits.
head: environment

label: lem:trunc-in-H
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:trunc-in-H}	
	If $G$ is a cubic graph in $\mathcal{H}$, then $\operatorname{T}(G)\in \mathcal{H}$.
head: environment

label: lem:trunc-ell
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:trunc-ell}
	For every edge \(\{u,v\}\) in a cubic graph \(G\), the corresponding edge \(\{u_v,v_u\}\) in~\(\operatorname{T}(G)\) satisfies~\(\ell(\{u_v,v_u\})= 2 \ell(\{u,v\})\).
head: environment

label: lem:trunc-edge-orbits
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:trunc-edge-orbits}	
	Let \(k \geq 3\) and \(G\) be a cubic graph such that all edges \(e\) of \(G\) satisfy \(\ell(e) = k\). Then the family \(\{\operatorname{T}^n(G)\}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}\) has an unbounded number of edge orbits.
head: environment

label: prop:many-ham-cyc
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:many-ham-cyc}	
	For every \(n \in \mathbb{N}\), there are graphs on~\(n\) vertices with~\(2^{\Theta(n \log n)}\) many Hamiltonian cycles up to symmetry.
head: environment

title: Conjecture
body_md: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite abelian group with generating set $S$ and let $G = \operatorname{Cay}(G,S)$. Then $G \in \mathcal{H}$ if and only if \(G \in \{C_4 \operatorname{\square} K_2, C_n, K_n, K_{n,n}, C_k \operatorname{\square} K_2 \colon n,k \in \mathbb{N}, k \text{ odd}\}\).
head: environment
